first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, making memory_31 (signup simplification) and memory_86 (shortening onboarding) directly relevant to the immediate degradation. Memory_73 (promotional pricing) is also verified because competitor pricing pressure creates a real risk that a discount-focused response could commoditize positioning and harm long-term revenue quality. However, simplify_onboarding addresses both the measurable activation decline AND preserves the ability to layer pricing or messaging later without cannibalizing core product value. Starting with a small_guarded_test on field reduction or flow streamlining lets us validate whether the prior lift still holds in current conditions before rolling out. This avoids premature reliance on price as a growth lever while protecting against further activation erosion.

final.rationale: Archive review confirms memory_31 is robust (+9% activation, +4% qualified revenue on SMB) with only minor retention risk (-1%). Memory_73 explicitly warns against promotional pricing as a sustainable lever: the -12% retention hit on acquired cohorts violates the primary objective of maximizing sustainable long-term qualified revenue. The current 6% activation decline and 4% onboarding decline map directly to the mechanisms memory_31 and memory_86 addressed. Simplify_onboarding as a standard_experiment scales the validated SMB playbook while avoiding the retention cliff of discounting. This preserves the option to layer enterprise_sales_assist or activation_messaging later if needed, maintains pricing integrity against competitor pressure, and directly addresses the measurable degradation. Uncertainty is preserved around segment specificity and magnitude of lift in current conditions.
